title: anim_engine command envelopes and payloads, schema version 1
description: The wire form of an envelope (spec 12.8) and of the twelve command payloads it carries (spec 12.2: every command payload type has a versioned JSON schema). Hand-authored, and checked against the bytes `anim_commands::registry::encode_command` actually writes by `the_committed_command_schema_matches_the_encoder` in crates/anim_commands/tests/atomicity.rs. That test compares the field sets, and `registry::payload_digest`'s own test covers the canonical stream, so this file and the dispatch table cannot drift apart silently. Dispatch is keyed on (kind, schema_version): a payload that needs a second shape registers a second handler rather than changing this file, and an envelope asking for a version the registry does not carry is refused as UnknownCommand naming both halves.

command_id.description: The idempotency handle (spec 12.5 step 5). Reoffering an accepted id with the same canonical envelope hash returns the original result; with a different hash it is a CommandReplayMismatch.

expected_scene_revision.description: The optimistic-concurrency check, named as spec 12.8 names it even though it is compared against the document's project-wide revision.

commands.description: Non-empty (spec 12.6), executed in this declared order, undone in the reverse order of their inverses.

upsert_asset.description: Spec 11.5 step 8's command: it commits a record `anim_assets::import` already returned. Its inverse is the record spec 11.6's reimport displaced, or `remove_asset` when nothing was displaced.

remove_asset.description: Refused while another record depends on it: `validate_manifest` reports the dangling edge rather than leaving a manifest that cannot resolve.

upsert_scene.description: Carries the whole scene, because the inverse of a replacement has to carry what was there.

add_node.description: Refused if the id is already in the scene: spec 10.8 generates an id once at creation.

remove_node.description: Refused while children or tracks refer to the node. Cascading would delete authored animation to complete one delete, and a subtree removed as a side effect cannot be restored by the one node this command's inverse carries.

set_property_key.description: Never creates a track as a side effect: if it did, the inverse of a first key would have to delete the track too, and one command would need two different inverses depending on state the caller did not choose. That is `upsert_track`.

place_marker.description: Refused when the same (position, label) pair is already there, so that the command either changes state or reports.
